_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: Advertising executive Alex Osborn began developing it in 1939.
beats.note: He popularised the term in his 1953 book, Applied Imagination.

beats.text: Go for quantity, withhold criticism, welcome wild ideas, combine and improve.
beats.note: He claimed groups would produce more ideas than people working alone.

beats.name: Taylor, Berry and Block
beats.role: Compared real groups of four with individuals working alone, whose ideas were pooled into pretend groups of four.

beats.text: The pooled individuals significantly outperformed the real groups.
beats.note: Later research blamed production blocking: only one person can speak at a time.

beats.context: Reviewed by Diehl and Stroebe in 1987. Groups brainstorming together produced fewer ideas than individuals working separately.
